# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 80 (Bi-Vb Pc80)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc80
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 80
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining without permission from family
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 80 (titled *Ananuññāta*) lays down an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for any nun who gives higher ordination (*vuṭṭhāpeti*) to a trainee nun (*sikkhamānā*) who has not received permission from her parents and/or husband [Bechert et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997]. In the non-offense clause (*anāpatti*), no offense is incurred if the nun ordains the trainee unknowingly (*ajānanti*) or after having sought authorization (*apaloketvā*) [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary *Samantapāsādikā* glosses *ajānanti* as ordaining without knowledge of the existence of the parents or guardians [Hüsken 1997]. While the Mahāvagga requires male candidates to obtain parental permission before lower ordination (*pabbajjā*), this rule requires a female candidate to secure permission from parents or husband immediately before her full ordination into the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha [Hüsken 1997].

 DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse with adjacent ordination rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, particularly Pācittiya 79, 81, 68, 16, 26, and 82, alongside an automatic cross-language alignment with the Sanskrit *Mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇīsūtra* [DharmaNexus].
